questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
It depends on the leather. He says to leave boots alone out of the box if they come pretreated, but to condition distressed or rustic leather. For frequency, his latest word (2022) is to treat them when they look or feel dry rather than on a fixed schedule.

**Out of the box**
- Reading Blundstone's FAQ, he notes that most Blundstones are pretreated, so the brand advises against treating them out of the box [1].
- The exception is rustic brown, Crazy Horse and rustic black leathers. They are distressed and don't carry the same pretreatment [2].
- For his own rustic pair, he says he "highly highly highly highly" recommends conditioning them rather than leaving them dry, even though that darkens the leather [3].

**How often**
- **Latest (2022):** He doesn't give a fixed schedule. He says he treats his boots when he feels they need it, and admits he probably does too little [4]. He says to use your intuition. If water isn't beading on top, you may need more wax; if the leather looks dry, it needs oil [5]. He also says to clean boots regularly, because dirt wears leather down faster [5].
- **Earlier (2019):** He was more cautious about upkeep. He said you may have to wax them every month, maybe every week if you're really hard on them, because the water resistance only lasts while they stay treated [6].

**Order**
He always goes in the order clean, condition, then wax [7].

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, the first wet soak or wash is what shrinks them, which is the point of shrink-to-fit. After that he finds they loosen with wear. His most recent advice (2025) is to size up two when you buy them [1]. In his 2023 comparison he says to skip very hot water and the dryer for a better fit [2].

**The first soak:**
- In 2025 he says to put them in the bathtub to shrink and to go two sizes up [1].
- In 2021 he says that if you size up two in the waist and two inches in length, the pants "fit regularly after you get them wet" [3].
- In his 2019 test, the jeans came out very tight in the waist after shrinking, but the length barely changed [4].

**Hot water and the dryer:**
- In 2023 he says a dryer would make them "a lot smaller" from the start [5].
- He says not to put them in the dryer or rinse them that hot, so you can "get a really nice fit" [2].
- The pair he didn't treat that way looked way better to him [2].

**After that, with wear:**
- A week after shrinking in 2019, the waist and upper thigh had stretched enough for him to wear a belt [6].
- In 2023 he guessed that frequent wear would stretch them to about the same size as regular rinsed 501s [7].

**Not covered:** he hasn't said exactly how much they tighten with ordinary washes after that first shrink. His 2023 remark is that if you wash them similarly, he doubts you'd notice a difference [5].

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
Going by his rule, a 33x30 in 502s would mean a **35 waist and a 32 length** in 501 STFs. That is my application of his advice. He hasn't compared 502 sizing to 501 STF sizing, so the 502 size is only your starting point.

**His rule (most recent first):**
- In 2025 he says you should usually go two sizes up in the shrink-to-fit 501 [1].
- In 2021 he spells it out: size up two in the waist and one length (two inches) longer. He says the pants then fit normally after you get them wet [2].
- In 2023 he shows this in practice: his 501 STFs were a size 32 against a size 30 in regular rinsed Levi's. He notes the STF waist doesn't follow vanity sizing, which is why you size up two [3].

**Caveats:**
- He admits a pair might not exist in the size the rule gives. His example is that a 34 wearer would need a 36, "although i don't think a 36 exists" [4]. He doesn't say what to do when the size is missing, so check that a 35 is available.
- He used to ignore Levi's advice. In 2019 he went down in size because jeans are usually too long on him [5]. By 2021 he said that was a mistake and that Levi's is correct. It took him four pairs of 501s to learn it [2].
- To avoid over-shrinking, he says not to put STFs in the dryer or soak them in very hot water. That gave him a really nice fit [6].

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
He cuffs mostly to fix length and to handle wide-legged jeans, though he has said he now sometimes prefers jeans worn over boots.

**Most recent (2020, Levi's 501 STF update):** He cuffed his 501s because he doesn't think his current style "lends itself to not cuffed wider legged pants" [1]. He also says he should have bought a 32 length instead of the 30 he got [1].

**Late 2019 (L.L. Bean boots):** He says he used to always cuff his jeans, but now likes them worn down over his boots. He thinks this calms the boots down as a loud fashion statement [2]. For a more workwear look, he recommends a 7 to 7.5 inch leg opening pulled down over the boot [3].

**Mid 2019 (first 501 video):** For him it's about length. If jeans look too long, he says, they just look bad, and that is the first thing he checks [4]. He also says the cuff can't be too thick [4]. Trying the unshrunk, wide 501s, he found a basic cuff and a pin roll both helped a little, though they were still wider than he likes [4][5].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
He used to say yes, but by 2023 he had hedged: he still calls the 3335s his favorite Red Wings on record, but says they "still might be but they probably not" now. He is also getting rid of them.

**2023 (latest):** He says he is on record that the 3335s are his favorite Red Wings of all time, "and they still might be but they probably not." He adds that the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [1]. What he likes about the 3335s is the stitch-down construction, the lighter weight, feeling more nimble, and being easier for walking or a light hike [1]. Even so, he is selling them as he culls his boot collection [1].

**2022 (earlier):** He was firmly in favor of the 3335s. He called them his favorite boots he's ever had and said they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s. His reasoning was that he's going for hikes and walks in the woods rather than doing heritage work. He called the 3335s a dramatically better all-around boot, and said they look way cooler [2]. He also said the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so anyone who needs a tough boot probably shouldn't go for the 3335s [2].

**Bottom line:** For hiking and walking, the 3335s were his pick over the 1907s in 2022. By 2023 he was no longer sure they're his favorite, and he was moving them on.

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of his latest video available here (September 2023), he is still a big fan of Blundstones. He is retiring his well-worn 585s, but that is a culling decision, not a verdict against the boot.

**Late 2023 (Sept 2023 boot-collection video)**
- He calls Blundstones "just incredible" and says he's "a big fan" who has "always loved them". He notes that some people don't like them [1].
- His 585s have held up and stayed "probably my most water resistant boots" [1]. He still says "it's time to retire those bunnies" [1].
- He is keeping a slip-on pair he can "flop on" quickly for errands or rain. He admits he "could easily put them on the sell list" [2].
- He had thought his heavy-duty Blundstone work boots were waterproof, but they are only very water-resistant nubuck [3].

**How his view got there**
- **2022:** He wrote "All in all I love Blundstones!" and called them "still some of my favorites". He also said they are not as repairable as Goodyear-welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines [4].
- **2020 (one-year review):** He thought they were decent for work but "not anything incredible". He said he would pick a smoother leather over the rustic nubuck if he did it again [5][6].
- **2019 (first review):** He recommended them "100%" if you will keep them treated [7].

He hasn't said anything about Blundstones after September 2023 in the videos available here.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He thinks Solovair is the better buy: it's cheaper and better built, with the leather and midsoles roughly equal to Made in England Docs. Made in England only wins if you specifically want the Dr. Martens name and look.

**Where he lands (2022 video, the only one that compares them directly)**
- **Price:** Solovairs are actually cheaper than Made in England Docs. [1]
- **Materials:** He says the Made in England Docs' better leather and midsoles are probably on par with Solovair's. [2]
- **Comfort and repair:** Solovairs have a shank, so they're a bit more comfortable over long periods. They're also Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, which makes them easier to resole. [3]
- **Same boot:** The Solovair derby eight-eyed boot is essentially the exact same boot as the Doc Martens. It's from the original maker, and the only thing it lacks is the yellow stitching. [4]
- **Verdict:** Unless the yellow stitching matters to you, he suggests going to Solovair. If it does, you have to get the Made in England Docs. [5]

**Caveat:** His own Solovairs had problems after eight wears: a back tab ripped off and a lace snapped. He assumes it was a manufacturing defect and expects the company to fix it. [6]

**His later view on Made in England (2023)**
In his later video he doesn't mention Solovair. He says the Made in England 1460 isn't worth the extra $90 over the Thailand pair on a purely robotic basis. He says you have to be a mega fan to get them. [7][8] This fits his earlier lean toward Solovair for anyone who isn't set on Docs specifically.

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't talked about multi-day hiking in Blundstones, so there's no direct verdict on a 4-day trip. His most recent word (2020) leans against them for serious mountain hiking, mainly because of ankle support.

**What he said about hiking in them (2020, after a year):**
- He says the boots "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1].
- He still took them up and down a few mountains in Maine. They got scuffed up but "held up well" [2].

**Water and care:**
- For wet ground, he says they're fine for crossing a brook or stream or standing in some mud for a bit [3].
- In 2019 he said to buy them knowing you'll have to look after the leather, because the water resistance depends on it staying treated [4].

**Applied to your trip:** He'd probably say they can handle day-hike conditions like mud and stream crossings. His one clear caveat is the lack of ankle support, which is likely to matter more over 4 days. He hasn't said how they hold up with a heavy pack or over several consecutive days.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** For a bigger build, he'd point you to the **Muji t-shirt**. His most recent word (Sept 2025) is that Uniqlo is the best t-shirt for the price, but if you're taller or wider you'd want Muji. He hasn't given a size recommendation for your height and weight.

**Why Muji for you**
- He calls the $20 Uniqlo "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. He then says that if you're taller or wider in any way, you'd want Muji [2].
- Muji costs about $4 or $5 more, but it is significantly longer and a good deal wider. It's slightly tented out, and he says you'd probably like it if you're a little bigger [2].
- In a June 2025 video he said Muji runs about $10 more than Uniqlo. He thought that was justified because it feels better, with a thicker, tighter collar and a bit of shine [3].

**Other value picks**
- **Uniqlo:** about $15 in the June 2025 video. It has a bound collar, and he said the price-to-quality ratio is "insane" [3]. He's less sure it will fit a bigger frame, since he steers taller or wider guys to Muji.
- **House of Blanks ($35, made in Canada):** zero torque (twisting after washing). He called it an outstanding value [4].
- **Front General Store ($40, made in Japan):** great proportions and feel [5].
- **Bronson ($29):** in June 2025 he said its standard loopwheel tubular tee would probably get the win over Bravestar [6]. In the 2025 roundup he noted Bronson usually wins or comes close in t-shirt comparisons [7].

**Size**
He hasn't said what size he'd pick for 5'11" and 225 lbs. His general fit taste is that he likes a lot of space across the shoulders [8]. For Los Angeles Apparel he said that if you size down one, it might win [9]. That tip is about that brand's cut, not your size.

questions.question: Is it my impression or RL has MUCH lower quality now than what it used to?

hybrid.answer:
The Iron Snail hasn't covered Ralph Lauren (RL) in the videos available here, so there's nothing from him on whether its quality has dropped.

The closest thing is his general take on "they don't make them like they used to" for other brands. On Levi's, he says modern ones aren't as far behind as people think: the difference in quality and durability between modern and vintage "is not as much as you probably would think" [1]. He also says that, at the same time, Levi's moved production to other countries and he assumes used a lower grade of cotton to hold the price [2].

In his Patagonia video, he argues that brands like L.L.Bean and Levi's cut quality once they went global, to make things faster and cheaper, and dropped things like lifetime warranties and customer service [3]. That's his view of those brands, not of Ralph Lauren.

questions.question: Where's Whitesville?? It's literally the most well known White Tee from Japan

Whitesville is in his videos, in both the t-shirt ranking and the sweatshirt ranking. He doesn't call it the best-known white tee from Japan. He describes it as a Japanese company riffing on old Americana underwear.

It was pre-washed, so he measured zero shrinkage [2].

**T-shirt ranking (Jul 2024):**
- He says it's cut like vintage tees, meaning underwear-style and very tight [3].
- He calls it "by far one of the softest t-shirts on the list" and says "I'd really recommend it" [3].
- He wasn't sold on the price until he looked at the collar. Binding tape over the collar helps it hold its shape over time [3].
- His shrink test was 5.4% in width and 3% in length [3].
- In his superlatives, Whitesville won the softest, coziest shirt award [4].

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** he says there's no single best tee, because it comes down to your preferences [1]. His most recent video still gives picks, though, so here is a short list drawn from them.

**If you buy just one:** Uniqlo at $20. He calls it "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [2]. It's his starter tee. If you're taller or wider, he says to get Muji instead, which is a few dollars more but longer and wider [3].

**If you want three, his winner-circle picks:**
- **Rougher, structured all-arounder:** J. Press x American Trench. He picks it over the 3Sixteen tee because he likes its rougher hand feel [4].
- **Clean, modern, smooth:** Merz b. Schwanen 2M15. It edged out Lady White for him that day, thanks to its smoother yarn and distinctive fit across the neck and chest [5].
- **Budget with character:** Front General Store, which he was "feeling" that day. If you'd rather have perfectly smooth with no twisting, he points to House of Blanks instead [6].

**Other options he has praised:**
- **Bronson:** He forgot to include it in his latest roundup, and says it usually wins or comes close in tee comparisons [7]. In mid-2025 he named its standard loopwheel tubular tee as his pick over Bravestar for value [8].
- **Asket:** It won his 2024 ranking [9], but it was left out of the 2025 list because that list was for tees under $50 [10].
- **Wonder Looper:** It was his Japan's might pick, mainly for its fit [11].

**How to decide:** if you like a rougher, more textured feel, go J. Press or Front General Store. If you like a silky, polished feel, go MSB or House of Blanks.

questions.question: Do you have any particular favorites for more athletic builds? I sometimes have trouble with high quality tees being tight on the shoulders and boxy around the waist

hybrid.answer:
The Iron Snail hasn't named a favorite for athletic builds, or for tight shoulders with a boxy waist. Going by his fit comments in the videos, though, a few shirts are worth a look, and a few are not.

**Worth trying**
- **Asket:** In his 2025 roundup he says this is what he imagines "very jacked or slim men wearing at coffee shops because it just flows, feels like glass, and it's beautiful." [1]
- **Wonder Looper (Japan's might pick):** He chose it over Samurai because it has "a much better fit, much more universal fit." [2]
- **J. Press x American Trench:** He likes a lot of room across the shoulders, so this is a good fit for him there. [3][4] He picked it as his favorite all-arounder. [5]
- **Whitesville:** In 2024 he called it "the jacked Instagram model special." It's cut like vintage underwear, so it's very tight. [6] If a snug cut suits your frame it may work, but that is the opposite of roomy and boxy-free in the shoulders.

**Likely to be a problem**
- **Samurai:** He calls it "cropped and wide," so it may not suit you. [2] He also says to size up one no matter what. [7]
- **Muji:** It's for people who are taller or wider. It's "significantly longer and a good deal wider" than Uniqlo. [8]
- **Velva Sheen:** In 2023 he said it fit him like "an extra small" and felt very small. [9]
- **Los Angeles Apparel:** It's very large and "fits me a bit like a tent." [10] He later said it might win if you size down one. [10]

He hasn't compared these shirts specifically for shoulder tightness against waist boxiness, so treat the above as general fit notes rather than athletic-build recommendations.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** He prefers the 1907 over the 875 if you're choosing a Red Wing moc toe. The 1907 has a storm welt, a removable leather footbed and leather laces, and costs about $10 more. He has since said that he likes both boots, and that his own favorite Red Wing is the 3335.

**His verdict (2021):** He calls the 1907s "red wings best heritage boots by far" and says to get them if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing [1].

**Construction**
- **875:** It has a Goodyear welt. He calls those welts "incredible" and says they are durable and pretty water resistant [2]. The welt leaves room for a cork footbed that molds to your foot over time [3].
- **1907:** It has a storm (Norwegian-like) welt, which he considers invaluable [4]. He notes that the popular view, which he saw on Reddit, is that Red Wing's storm welt isn't that complex. It is apparently just another strip of leather stitched onto the welt, and he isn't sure about it himself [5].

**Price and extras:** The 1907 costs $10 more, but he argues the difference is smaller than that [6]. The 1907 includes Red Wing's inner leather footbed, which he says typically sells separately for $40 [4]. It also comes with leather laces [4]. In his math, the extra $10 gets you about $45 of extras net [7].

**Waterproofing:** In his 2021 test, one 1907 leaked almost immediately through the stitching, which he found a letdown. The other boot stayed dry. He still has "no doubt" they would hold up fine in rain, grass or mud [8].

**What they share:** Both have crepe soles, and in 2022 he said the soles on the 875 and 1907 wear down faster than the Vibram sole on the 3335 [9]. He also called both "more beefily constructed", so they suit you if you need a tough boot [10].

**Later view:** In 2022 he said his favorite boots are the 3335s, which beat both the 1907 and the 875 [10]. In 2023 he said the 875s, the 1907s and the Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [11].

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** In his latest take (Sept 2025), Uniqlo is the best budget t-shirt. He says the $20 Uniqlo is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. Front General Store is a step up in price and a great shirt, but he doesn't rank it above Uniqlo on value. He hasn't compared Uniqlo directly with Pro Club or Hanes.

**Uniqlo**
- In 2025 he calls it a rough, open-end "starter t-shirt". He suggests Muji instead if you're taller or wider, since Muji is longer and wider [2].
- In mid-2025 he praised the $15 version for its bound neck collar, which doesn't wiggle, and said the price-to-quality ratio is insane [3].
- In 2024 he said that if you're after a heavyweight, coarse-feeling tee with a bound, ribbed collar, he highly recommends it, and that it may be the best bargain tee [4].
- In June 2025 he put Bronson and Bravestar "neck and neck" on value, slightly above Uniqlo [5].

**Front General Store**
- It costs about $38–40 and is made in Japan. In 2025 he described it as having "great proportions, great feel" [6], and called it "still really good" [7].
- In 2024 he called it "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get" if you want a Japanese-made upgrade for under $40. He rated its softness 6 out of 10 [8].
- In short, it's the nicer upgrade, but it costs about twice as much as Uniqlo.

**Pro Club (2024)**
- He liked everything about it, but called it the roughest shirt on that list and gave it a softness of 4 out of 10 [9].

**Hanes (2024)**
- He called it "your classic $10 great shirt" and gave it a softness of 7 out of 10 [10]. He also said it was much softer than the Pro Club [11].

**Bottom line:** Uniqlo is his pick for budget overall. Hanes is the cheapest option he praised, and he rated it softer than Pro Club. Front General Store is the one to buy if you'll spend about $40 for Japanese-made. He gave Uniqlo no softness score, so he hasn't ranked it against Hanes or Pro Club on that.

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
Assuming "this" means the Barbour, he'd lean Barbour for that mix of rain, wind and spring use. He never compares the two head to head, and he doesn't directly rate either one as a windbreaker.

**Barbour (his 2025 take)**
- He says it isn't a designated rain jacket, but it uses the lightest-weight fabric of the jackets in his ranking: 6 oz Sylkoil. [1]
- He says that flexibility means you can toss it on in fall, summer or spring, "any time of year", and be comfortable. [2]
- For bad weather it has storm cuffs, a throat latch and snaps for a hood. [3]
- Back in 2021 he found his new Bedale didn't leak at all in a shower, but he calls waxed jackets "very very very water-resistant when they are properly treated", not waterproof. [4]
- The catch is upkeep. As the wax wears and the patina develops, it gets less water resistant. [5]

**Flint and Tinder**
- He calls it "a lighter weight" jacket, though "not crazy lightweight", cut well for freedom of movement and lined so you don't get wax on your skin. [6]
- He says it's built for everyone and, at $300, is hard not to recommend. It's US-made, in Martexin fabric. [7]
- He doesn't mention a hood or storm cuffs on it, and he doesn't test its rain or wind performance in the videos available here.

**Bottom line:** For a single jacket that has to handle rain, wind and light spring layering, his comments favor the Barbour. It has the lightest fabric, a hood and storm cuffs, and he praises its year-round wearability. The Flint and Tinder is the easy, comfortable lined everyday pick, but he hasn't said it's built for rain or wind. If you go Barbour, expect to re-wax it to keep the water resistance.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
His 2023 review called the unlined build a con, but by 2025 he describes the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker from Huckberry as lined, so the lined versions you mention fit his later view. He hasn't said whether the lined jacket is a different version from the one he reviewed in 2023, and he doesn't mention a flannel-lined one.

**2023 (the video you're asking about):** He reviewed the Huckberry Waxed Trucker as the cheapest, simplest, unlined jacket of the group, at $228 [1]. He says his one con for it, and for the Rogue Territory, is that they aren't lined [2]. He explains that he personally always likes a lining on waxed jackets so the wax isn't touching your clothes or arms [2].

**2025:** In the sponsored Huckberry segment, he calls the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker lined, which keeps wax off your skin [3]. He mentions a wool-lined version he hasn't yet tried, which he says is heavier overall [3]. He also notes the price is now $300 for a lined, US-made jacket in Martexin fabric [4]. That segment was paid by Huckberry, though he says he had praised the jacket many times before the sponsorship [5].

**His general stance on lining has also softened.** In 2025 he says he still usually wants a liner on waxed jackets, but "in my old age" he sees why you wouldn't line one. He says satin sleeves can limit how often you can wear the jacket, because they get sticky when it's warm [6].

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
He doesn't compare the fit of the 3335s and 875s directly in the videos available here. He does say the 3335s fit true to size but run slim and tapered, and that Red Wings in general should be bought snug.

**3335 fit:** He went true to size and says they "fit fine." He notes the profile is very slim, the outsole is very thin, and the boots taper down. With thin cotton socks in warm weather he felt no tightness. With wool socks his toes felt squished and he couldn't wiggle them much [1].

**Red Wing sizing in general:** In his 1907 video he usually wears an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings, and says they fit perfect. His rule is to buy leather boots snug but not squished, because the leather will mold to your feet [2].

**The 875:** He doesn't give sizing or fit details for the 875 in these videos. He only says the 875s and 1907s are more "beefily constructed" than the 3335s [3]. That is about toughness, not fit. If you wear wool socks, his 3335 comments suggest you might want to allow for the tapered toe.
